headline: High-risk shared filesystem and unsandboxed server-side code make Langflow→mem0 interactions dangerous by default; prompt injection and cascading errors are also plausible.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Langflow can read and write server filesystem content and chain multiple agents; mem0 is a knowledge-management component that may ingest outputs as memory. A shared workspace or copied outputs create a plausible injection path, though no direct shared channel is documented. Uncertainty about the exact bridge pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Langflow flow outputs are written to files that mem0 later ingests
IF mem0 treats Langflow-generated text as trusted memory without sanitization
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different workspaces
Disable automatic ingestion of raw flow outputs into memory
Add provenance tags to all Langflow outputs
Review any file-based handoff before enabling it
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlist parsing

B_data_leakage.rationale: Langflow touches flow inputs, intermediate outputs, uploaded files, and per-flow credentials, while mem0 is a memory store with no stated egress. If they share a workspace or server-side state, sensitive flow data can leak into memory outputs. The lack of explicit isolation or retention controls makes medium the safest choice.
conditions: IF Langflow stores uploaded files or secrets in shared server-side state
IF mem0 persists memory derived from Langflow flow inputs or intermediate outputs
mitigations: Store secrets outside shared flow artifacts
Restrict mem0 ingestion to redacted summaries
Use separate principals or workspaces
Set explicit retention limits on memory writes
requires-engineering: implement field-level redaction before persistence

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Langflow has broad filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and network egress; mem0 has no declared write or egress capability, but the pair can still contend over shared mutable resources if deployed together. Because Langflow explicitly supports shared server-side state and multiple instances, coordination bugs are plausible even without mem0 write details. Uncertainty warrants medium.
conditions: IF both agents are deployed against the same directory or shared store
IF Langflow instances run concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Disable concurrent writes to shared artifacts
Add a lock file or mutex around shared resources
Avoid git or database mutation from the shared path
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow can generate intermediate outputs from chained agents, and mem0 can store or reuse those outputs as memory. If mem0 treats Langflow output as authoritative, an upstream hallucination or malformed instruction can cascade into later decisions. No verification mechanism is documented in either profile, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF mem0 stores Langflow outputs without verification
IF downstream flows read memory entries as authoritative facts
mitigations: Require human review for memory writes
Mark Langflow outputs as untrusted by default
Add a verification step before persistence
Limit memory writes to extracted entities only
requires-engineering: add confidence scoring and provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, but Langflow handles flow inputs, intermediate outputs, and stored credentials, while mem0 is a memory system with unspecified retention and residency. The profiles do not show a concrete residency or certification mismatch, so only a low compliance concern is supported. The other agent is cited because the risk is about data flowing between them.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Langflow flows and then persisted by mem0
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the two systems
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared flows
Document retention settings for both systems
Delete test memories after validation
Use separate datasets for regulated content
requires-engineering: align residency and deletion controls
